decision.reasoning: Two findings are failing right now: picture_area (the recorded picture is 1620×1080 inside a 1920×1080 file at +150+0 — it is pillarboxed) and subject_size (shoulders span p50 0.501, p95 0.622, against the 0.55 cap; holding size requires moving the head down to 0.413). Both are squarely addressed by the fix.reframe strategy, which is listed under 'addresses': ["picture_area", "subject_size"]. No other failing gate exists at this point (pose_coverage is pass at 0.998, one_subject is pass at 0.999, face_exposure is pass at 1.059). The distance_steady and headroom findings are warnings — recorded-content limits that cannot be fixed downstream and are not defects to resolve. fix.reframe is cheap and has not been tried yet (attempts_so_far is empty, fixes_applied is empty, retry_budget is 2). The strategy's bounds (head_target_max 0.55, scale_tol 0.25) are consistent with the profile framing parameters. If this fix does not bring subject_size within the 0.55 cap — for example because the close-up frames (p95 0.622) persist beyond what the scale tolerance can accommodate — and the gate still fails after processing, the honest next step would be reshoot with subject_size and distance_steady guidance (stand 2–3 m from the camera, do not walk toward it, be at final distance before the take starts).

The fix.reframe has already been applied and all measurable gates are now showing pass status in the current findings: picture_area passes (1620×1080 cropped), pose_coverage passes at 0.998 (≥0.6), one_subject passes at 0.999 (≥0.95), subject_size passes with p50 0.442 and p95 0.548 (≤0.55 cap), and face_exposure passes at 1.059× (within the 0.8–1.25 clamp). The two remaining items — distance_steady (1.75× apparent size ratio, warn threshold ≤1.35) and headroom (crown cut on 76% of frames) — are recorded as warnings, not gate failures; the rules state warnings are recorded-content limits for the report, not defects to fix, and no allowed strategy can undo the perspective walk or invent the unrecorded crown rows. No verification has been run yet (latest_verification is null) and no process attempt has been made (attempts_so_far is empty, reprocesses_used is 0). The profile's process.standard strategy is the standard strategy for a first attempt and carries no gate-address restriction. With 2 retries remaining and 0 used, the budget supports this. If the standard render passes all gates in verification, we deliver; if separation or another gate fails, process.separation_targeted is still available as a retry.

The latest verification (attempt_1, process.standard) failed two gates: head_spread at 0.029 against a ceiling of 0.02, and head_drift at 5.3 px against a ceiling of 4.0 px. Both failures are caused by the performer walking toward the camera — the distance_steady finding shows apparent size changing 1.75× across the take, and the headroom finding confirms the crown leaves the picture on 76 % of frames. These are recorded-content problems: the reframe fix has already been applied (fix.reframe is consumed from fixes_applied), and no remaining allowed strategy in the profile addresses head_spread or head_drift. process.separation_targeted addresses only the separation gate (which already passes at 1.72×), so using it would not fix the failing gates. process.standard has already been run and failed. The retry budget shows 0 reprocesses used against a budget of 2, but there is simply no strategy available that addresses the root cause — camera movement baked into the source. A reshoot is the only honest exit. The performer must stand still at their final distance before the take starts (2–3 m from the camera, head to mid-thigh framing), must not walk toward or away from the camera during the take, and must export without pillarbox padding.
